content.content:
entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

Both backends act as ENTIRE_TOKEN when set, else the selected login
(--context, else $ENTIRE_CONTEXT, else the active context), so a staging
login reaches staging's control plane and cells. The cell host comes from
environment's cluster listing; an explicit ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL names the
data host directly instead.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters

content.text:
CI is green. "Verify Marvin" passes on `9728161`, for both the push and the pull request run, with all three jobs (software, firmware, simulator-performance-gate) passing. On the trail, checks and up-to-date now pass. Only the approvals gate is still open, which needs a reviewer.

The simulator work had nothing to do with it. Two web end-to-end tests were the problem, and both were problems in the tests, not the app:

1. **`tests/e2e/pet-conversation.spec.ts`** had failed on every run since at least September 28, on `main` too. The app creates and selects a new conversation asynchronously, but the test read the selected conversation straight after clicking "New conversation". On CI's slower machines that read still returned the previous conversation. CI's own trace showed the new conversation had in fact been created.
   - The test now takes the new conversation's ID from the server's response and waits until that row is selected.
   - To check the fix, I slowed that request down by 800 ms locally. The old test then fails with exactly CI's error, and the new one passes.

2. **`tests/e2e/portal.spec.ts`** would have failed next; CI never got there because the suite stops at the first failing file. Its eight tests together make about 190 API requests within a minute, against the server's limit of 200 per client per minute. Its last test kept hitting 429 "Too Many Requests" and showed a blank page; locally that happened in 2 of 3 runs.
   - The test runner gives each file its own server so that the production limit stays as it is. So I split the file instead of raising the limit: the streaming, appearance and repository explorer tests moved to a new file, `tests/e2e/portal-flows.spec.ts`.

Locally, `npm run check` passes, and the full suite passed 25 of 25 tests three times in a row with Node 22.16, the version CI uses. I didn't run the Postgres tests locally because they need a database; they pass on CI.

**`main` is still red.** Both tests fail there the same way, and the fix is only on this branch, so `main` turns green when the branch is merged.

content.content:
entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

  -f, --force            Skip confirmation and amend the last commit with the checkpoint trailer (best-effort; if the amend fails the checkpoint is still created and the trailer is printed for manual paste)

content.content:
branch rather than blindly reusing a historical name or pushing to main.
- Attach the appropriate **Entire session and checkpoint trailer** to commits and
  verify both the commit and checkpoint reached the remote. A local success
  message or a trailer alone does not prove a remote session is available.
- Use the supported attachment flow for the current session. Do not fabricate a
  checkpoint ID, reuse another session's ID, or claim that reattaching an existing
  checkpoint proves the latest transcript was newly captured. Disclose that
  distinction where relevant.
- The user previously authorized hook approval and later requested an empty
  provenance commit when hooks were unavailable. Do not repeatedly tell the user
  to run `/hooks`: it was not valid in this desktop environment, and the user
  could not open a separate CLI. Check actual capabilities and permissions;
  report a real blocker honestly and use supported attachment alternatives.
- An empty provenance commit was a specific repair request, not a requirement
  for every change. Never claim hooks are approved without evidence.
